WebApplicationClient constructor arguments swapped causing incorrect client_id assignment

#### Description

When creating a WebApplicationClient instance, the client_id and code parameters appear to be swapped internally, causing the client_id to be stored as the code and vice versa. This results in incorrect behavior when preparing authorization requests and token requests.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from oauthlib.oauth2 import WebApplicationClient

# Create a client with a specific client_id
client = WebApplicationClient('my_client_id')

# Try to prepare a request URI - this should include the client_id in the URL
uri = client.prepare_request_uri('https://example.com/auth')
print("Generated URI:", uri)
# Expected: https://example.com/auth?client_id=my_client_id&response_type=code
# Actual: Incorrect client_id value appears

# Check what's actually stored
print("Client ID:", client.client_id)
print("Code:", client.code)
# Expected: Client ID: my_client_id, Code: None
# Actual: Values are swapped
```

The issue also affects token request preparation where the wrong values are used for authentication and authorization code exchange.
</issue>
